title: Finance Minister Says Iran War Has Added 7 Points to Turkey's Inflation
detail: Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek raised his estimate of the US-Israel-Iran war's effect on Turkey's annual inflation to at least 7 percentage points, up from the 5-point estimate he gave in June, citing higher oil, natural gas and commodity prices that hit Turkey harder because inflation was already elevated. Şimşek said annual inflation would have ended 2026 around 21–22% without the war; the government has instead raised its year-end forecast to 28.4%, up from a 16% projection made a year earlier and from 26% just last month.

media.caption: Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek revises up the war's inflationary impact

title: Turkish FM Fidan Warns Greek Military Presence on Kastellorizo Violates Demilitarized Status
detail: Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, speaking during a visit to Azerbaijan, said 'the militarization of the islands that have a demilitarized status constitutes a threat for us,' after Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis visited Kastellorizo — 2km off Turkey's south coast — and nearby military outposts on September 11–13. Turkey's Defense Ministry said the visit and Greek troop presence violate the island's demilitarized status under the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne and 1947 Paris Peace Treaty; Greece rejects Ankara's legal interpretation and says it will defend its islands. Turkish media reported Turkey had relocated its 51st Commando Brigade opposite the Greek island of Samos. Both countries are NATO members with a long-running dispute over Aegean maritime boundaries and airspace.

media.caption: Turkey warns Greek military activity on the demilitarized island of Kastellorizo

title: Data Breaches at 12 Turkish Companies Expose Records of Over 10 Million People
detail: Turkey's Personal Data Protection Authority (KVKK) published 12 breach notices disclosing that security incidents at 12 companies exposed the personal data of a combined 10,218,802 customers and employees (an 11-company count; a 12th company had not yet determined its total). The largest was at cosmetics retailer Eve Kozmetik, affecting 6,263,305 customers after attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party software library on a data processor's server; retailer Shaya Mağazacılık reported 2,298,726 affected and boutique chain Deniz Butik reported 1,271,096. Exposed data included names, email addresses, phone numbers and, in some cases, home addresses and login credentials. KVKK said reviews of the breaches are continuing.

media.caption: Turkey's data protection regulator discloses breaches affecting over 10 million people
